reason: The page contains durable endpoint-specific semantics that are not merely navigational: it defines uniqueness enforcement and its failure behavior, identifies downstream invoice propagation, specifies required request fields, and enumerates the supported managed entity values. Treating it only as a raw reference would omit facts needed to implement and reason about the API contract.
risk: If this page remains navigation-only, future answers may miss the duplicate-value failure condition, omit the required enforce_uniqueness field, over- or under-state supported entity types, or fail to account for which custom fields propagate to invoices.
missed_durable_facts: A custom field key can enforce uniqueness, and setting a value already used for that key fails.
Custom fields on customers, contracts, invoices, products, commits, scheduled charges, and subscriptions are passed down to the invoice.
The add-key request requires entity, key, and enforce_uniqueness; key is a string and enforce_uniqueness is a boolean.
The ManagedEntity schema enumerates the supported entity identifiers, including alert, billable_metric, customer, contract, invoice, product, subscription, and package-level entity types.

grounding_quotes.text: Creates a new custom field key for a given entity (e.g. billable metric, contract, alert).
grounding_quotes.supports: The endpoint creates a custom field key for a specified Metronome entity.

grounding_quotes.text: - Specify whether the key should enforce uniqueness. If the key is set to enforce uniqueness and you attempt to set a custom field value for the key that already exists, it will fail.
grounding_quotes.supports: Uniqueness enforcement has an explicit duplicate-value failure behavior.

grounding_quotes.text: - Custom fields for customers, contracts, invoices, products, commits, scheduled charges, and subscriptions are passed down to the invoice.
grounding_quotes.supports: Custom fields on the listed entity types propagate to invoices.

              properties:

                key:
